11 minutes|yungblud \u0026 halsey (feat..note: Released in February 2019, '11 Minutes' brings together the distinct alt-rock and pop-punk energies of YUNGBLUD, Halsey, and blink-182 drummer Travis Barker for a high-energy collaboration. For listeners drawn to heavy drum beats and modern takes on classic pop-punk, the track delivers massive hooks and a genre-blending style.

barrel of a gun|guster.note: "Barrel of a Gun" is a track by Boston-formed alternative rock band Guster, featured on their 1995 sophomore album "Goldfly." For fans who caught them opening for Barenaked Ladies in the mid-'90s, the song's distinctive acoustic guitars, hand percussion, and memorable "4, 3, 2, 1" hook capture the early sound of the trio before they expanded their setup.

brick|ben folds five.note: Released in 1997 as part of Ben Folds Five's sophomore album Whatever and Ever Amen, "Brick" became the band's highest-charting single on the Modern Rock Tracks chart. Standing out during an era dominated by heavy alternative and grunge, the piano-driven track helped cement the trio's unique place in late-90s rock.

colors|halsey.note: Released as the third single from Halsey's 2015 debut studio album 'Badlands', 'Colors' is a synth-heavy pop track that resonates with fans of melodic, retro-inspired alternative music.

deep cover|dr. dre and snoop dogg.note: Released in 1992 as the lead single from the soundtrack to the film of the same name, 'Deep Cover' marked Dr. Dre's solo debut following the breakup of N.W.A and famously introduced the world to Snoop Dogg. The minimalist, bass-heavy G-funk beat provided the perfect backdrop for Snoop's effortless flow and laid the groundwork for their legendary collaboration on 'The Chronic'.

demons|imagine dragons.note: Released in 2013 as part of Imagine Dragons' debut studio album 'Night Visions', 'Demons' became a massive radio staple of the 2010s and peaked at number six on the US Billboard Hot 100. Its ubiquitous presence made it a memorable soundtrack for everything from sports games to family car rides.

dreams|van halen.note: Released in 1986 as the second single from Van Halen's album 5150, "Dreams" showcased the band's innovative use of synthesizers alongside hard rock guitars. The track peaked at number 22 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and marked a defining moment for the band's new era with vocalist Sammy Hagar, resonating with listeners who discovered it on MTV during their middle school years.

enjoy the silence|depeche mode.note: Released in 1990 on the landmark album Violator, Depeche Mode's 'Enjoy the Silence' became one of the defining synth-pop tracks of the MTV era. Driven by its iconic melodic guitar hook layered over electronic beats, the single reached number six on the UK Singles Chart and became a staple for fans graduating high school that year.

freshman|verve pipe.note: Released in 1996 as the third single from The Verve Pipe's album 'Villains', 'The Freshman' became the band's most successful commercial hit, reaching the top five on the US Billboard Modern Rock Tracks and Billboard Hot 100 Airplay charts. For this listener, the song is deeply tied to the memory of a pivotal college-era breakup and a night spent staying at a friend's place for the very first time.

heartspark dollarsign|everclear.note: "Heartspark Dollarsign" is a single by the alternative rock band Everclear, originally appearing on their 1995 debut album World of Noise and later re-recorded for their major-label debut Sparkle and Fade. This track brings back powerful memories for a listener who heard them perform it during a memorable Boston holiday concert near the end of their college years.

here comes a regular|the replacements.note: Originally released on The Replacements' acclaimed 1985 album Tim, "Here Comes a Regular" is a poignant acoustic ballad written by Paul Westerberg that has since become a fan favorite. For this listener, the track evokes memories of a vacation to Wilmington with Mike and Jess—a city beloved both for its connection to One Tree Hill and as a late musical discovery made nearly 15 years after the album's release.

hey ya|outkast.note: Released in 2003 as part of Outkast's ambitious double album Speakerboxxx/The Love Below, 'Hey Ya!' became a massive cultural phenomenon and spent nine consecutive weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100. Its groundbreaking music video, which featured André 3000 performing on a fictional British television show reminiscent of The Ed Sullivan Show, remains an iconic visual touchstone of the era. For this listener, the track's infectious energy serves as a nostalgic soundtrack tied to holding their newborn son and working out while he slept.

home sweet home|mötley crüe.note: Released in 1985 on Mötley Crüe's album *Theatre of Pain*, "Home Sweet Home" helped define the era of the power ballad in heavy metal. The song became a staple of MTV and reached number 89 on the Billboard Hot 100, capturing the bittersweet feeling of moving on that resonates with listeners transitioning into middle school.

i write sins not tragedies|panic! at the.note: Released in 2005 by Las Vegas band Panic! At The Disco, "I Write Sins Not Tragedies" became a defining anthem of the mid-2000s emo and theatrical rock wave, peaking at number seven on the US Billboard Hot 100. As you noted, its massive hooks and memorable music video made it stand out alongside tracks like Fall Out Boy's "Thnks fr th Mmrs."

i'll be|edwin mccain.note: Released in 1997 on Edwin McCain's album 'Messenger', 'I'll Be' became a major adult contemporary hit and reached number 35 on the US Billboard Hot 100. For this listener, the track serves as a nostalgic backdrop to the bittersweet era of college roommates scattering to different states to start families and new lives.

joey|concrete blonde.note: Released in 1990 by the alternative rock band Concrete Blonde, 'Joey' became the band's biggest commercial hit, reaching number 19 on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart. For this listener, the track evokes nostalgic memories of discovering the song through the early years of the TV show 90210 and driving around southeastern Massachusetts to visit his first girlfriend, who is now his wife.

love song|the cure.note: Released in 1989 as the second single from The Cure's landmark eighth studio album, *Disintegration*, 'Lovesong' became the band's highest-charting single on the US Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number two. Driven by its lush, modern arrangements and iconic guitar work, the track remains a defining masterpiece of British alternative music.

mayonaise|smashing pumpkins.note: "Mayonaise" is a standout track from The Smashing Pumpkins' critically acclaimed 1993 sophomore album, *Siamese Dream*. Known for its dynamic shifts between acoustic melancholy and massive, layered distorted guitar walls, it remains one of the band's most beloved songs among fans, including those who shared the album in their college rooms around the era of Lollapalooza.

monsters (feat. blackbear)|all time low.note: Bridging All Time Low's signature pop-punk sound with contemporary hip-hop elements, "Monsters" featuring blackbear became a massive crossover hit following its 2020 release. The track spent a record-breaking number of weeks at number one on the Billboard Alternative Airplay chart, reflecting the modern stylistic shifts you appreciate in their recent work.

more than words|extreme.note: Extreme's acoustic ballad "More than Words" became a defining anthem for high school proms and graduations, capturing the bittersweet feeling of moving on to college. Released in 1990 on the album *Extreme II: Pornograffitti*, the song famously reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 in 1991 for the Boston-based rock band.

my name is jonas|weezer.note: Serving as the opening track to Weezer's iconic 1994 self-titled debut, known as the Blue Album, 'My Name Is Jonas' captures the band's signature dynamic shift from delicate acoustic picking into soaring, heavy guitars. Released during the era of alternative rock's dominance, the track helped cement the geek-rock aesthetic and became an enduring fan favorite just as the listener was finishing college.

nightswimming|r.e.m..note: Released in 1993 as the fourth single from R.E.M.'s critically acclaimed album Automatic for the People, 'Nightswimming' features a poignant piano-and-oboe arrangement driven by lead singer Michael Stipe's evocative nostalgia. For this listener, the track holds a deeply personal connection, serving as close college friends' wedding song and a nostalgic reminder of happiness, love, and friendship.

papercut|linkin park.note: Released as the third single from Linkin Park's diamond-certified 2000 debut album *Hybrid Theory*, "Papercut" is renowned for its seamless fusion of aggressive rap-rock, electronic scratching, and grunge-influenced guitar grit. This unique sonic bridge between hip-hop and rock resonates deeply with listeners who grew up straddling different musical and cultural worlds during a period of major personal transition.

regret|new order.note: Released in 1983... wait, no. Released in 1993, New Order's "Regret" became the band's final major Billboard Hot 100 hit, bridging their classic synth-pop origins with modern alternative rock sensibilities. For this listener, the track evokes memories of 1993 college dorm life, shared through a roommate's love of British alternative alongside '90s grunge.

scenario|a tribe called quest.note: Released in 1992 on A Tribe Called Quest's acclaimed sophomore album "The Low End Theory," "Scenario" is widely celebrated for its hard-hitting production and for featuring Busta Rhymes' legendary breakout guest verse. Despite the rise of grunge dominating the musical landscape of the early '90s, this iconic track remained a staple rotation for rap fans, perfectly capturing the vibrant energy of college dorm life and youth culture.

silent running|mike + the mechanics.note: Mike + The Mechanics released "Silent Running" in late 1985 as the lead single from their self-titled debut album, eventually propelling it to number six on the US Billboard Hot 100 in early 1986. For this listener, the atmospheric keyboards of the track evoke powerful nostalgia for Prospect Street, childhood friendships, and the memorable 1986 Patriots football season.

smells like teen spirit|nirvana.note: Released in 1991 as the lead single from Nirvana's seminal album Nevermind, 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' became an anthem of the grunge movement and famously propelled alternative rock into the mainstream by topping charts worldwide. For this listener, the track serves as a powerful soundtrack to dorm life, reflecting the shifts in trajectory caused by freshman-year choices and the bittersweet reality of childhood friends moving on.

so what'cha want|beastie boys.note: Released in 1992 as the lead single from the Beastie Boys' third album, Check Your Head, 'So What'Cha Want' bridged the gap between their hardcore punk roots and hip-hop. Reconnecting with these gritty rock textures, the track resonates with listeners who watched the band adapt to the changing 1990s musical landscape and paved the way for future rap-rock fusions.

someday i suppose|mighty mighty bosstone.note: Released in 1993 on the album "Don't Know How to Party," the Mighty Mighty Bosstones' "Someday I Suppose" is a defining track of the 1990s ska-core movement that originated in Boston. Capturing the intense, high-energy, and catchy sound of the band, the song serves as a fitting soundtrack for the listener's memories of a sweaty, pipe-dripping New Year's Eve concert at Cambridge's legendary Middle East club.

something's always wrong|toad the wet sp.note: "Something's Always Wrong" is a single by alternative rock band Toad the Wet Sprocket, released on their 1994 album *Dulcinea*, which peaked at number 34 on the US Billboard 200. For this listener and their college best friends, the track serves as a soundtrack to enduring friendships and unforgettable shows at venues like the Orpheum Theater, remaining a constant source of happiness from their twenties to the present.

somewhere only we know|keane.note: Released in 2004 as the lead single from Keane's debut album "Hopes and Fears," "Somewhere Only We Know" became a defining melodic piano-rock anthem of the 2000s and later found a new generation of fans through television features like "Glee." It peaked at number three on the UK Singles Chart and remains celebrated for its soaring, memorable hooks.

summer|buffalo tom.note: Buffalo Tom released "Summer" on their acclaimed 1992 album "Let Me Come Over," a record that helped cement the Boston alternative rock band's reputation for driving, melodic guitar anthems. For this listener, the song is deeply intertwined with a bittersweet memory: seeing the band live one last time before a friend moved to Arizona, a night made unforgettable when Greg was pulled up onto the stage.

teenage love|slick rick.note: Released in 1988 on Slick Rick's acclaimed debut album *The Great Adventures of Slick Rick*, "Teenage Love" captures the awkwardness and earnest longing of youth that resonated deeply with listeners navigating high school.

the old apartment|barenaked ladies.note: Released in 1996 as part of Barenaked Ladies' album Born on a Pirate Ship, 'The Old Apartment' became one of the band's signature alternative rock hits, peaking at number one on the Canadian RPM Alternative 30 chart.

there is a light that never goes out|the.note: Introduced to you by your junior year college roommate, "There is a Light That Never Goes Out" by The Smiths is celebrated for its brilliant, witty lyricism and Morrissey's trademark swagger. Although not released as a proper single during the band's initial run, the track became a defining anthem of 1980s British alternative rock and a fan favorite.

thnks fr th mmrs|fall out boy.note: Released in 2007 as part of Fall Out Boy's album "Infinity on High," "Thnks fr th Mmrs" became a major mainstream hit, peaking at number 11 on the Billboard Hot 100. Its infectious energy and memorable hooks make it a defining track of the mid-2000s pop-punk era. For fans of the era, the song also evokes nostalgic memories of shows like "One Tree Hill," which famously featured the band.

tiny dancer|elton john.note: Released in 1971 on Elton John's album 'Madman Across the Water', 'Tiny Dancer' has become a classic rock staple, famously featured in the 2000 film 'Almost Famous' during a memorable tour bus scene that resonates with your personal connection to the song, its harmonies, and characters.

title and registration|death cab for cut.note: "Title and Registration" is a standout track from Death Cab for Cutie's 2003 breakthrough major-label debut album, *Transatlanticism*. Known for its witty observations about stumbling across souvenirs in a glove compartment, the melodic indie rock song remains a fan favorite, resonating with listeners who discovered the band during their memorable era in the mid-2000s.

welcome to the terrordome|public enemy.note: Released in 1989 as the lead single from Public Enemy's landmark album 'Fear of a Black Planet', 'Welcome to the Terrordome' is celebrated for its dense, high-energy production and intricate lyricism. For this listener, the track evokes nostalgic memories of car rides to the amusement park with family, alongside the enduring impact of discovering hip-hop through their cousin.

with or without you|u2.note: Released in 1987 on U2's landmark album The Joshua Tree, "With or Without You" became the band's first number-one single on the US Billboard Hot 100. During your time living in Boston, the song resonated deeply within the city's heavily Irish-influenced local music scene, capturing the track's immense emotional power and soaring musical arrangement.

would|alice in chains.note: "Would?" served as the lead single for Alice in Chains' critically acclaimed 1992 sophomore album, *Dirt*, and was prominently featured on the soundtrack to Cameron Crowe's Seattle-set film *Singles*. Written by guitarist Jerry Cantrell as a tribute to the late Mother Love Bone singer Andrew Wood, the track has become an enduring anthem of the grunge era.
